v1.question: How many days do I have to submit a reimbursement claim after discharge?
v1.answer: For retail reimbursement claims, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. For Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the reimbursement submission deadline is 60 days from discharge [4].
v1.gold_answer: 30 days from the date of discharge.

v1.question: What is the room rent limit on the Silver plan?
v1.answer: Under the Aurora Silver plan, the room rent limit is 2% of the sum insured per day [4][5].
v1.gold_answer: 2% of the sum insured per day.

v1.question: Is maternity covered on the Bronze plan?
v1.answer: No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].
v1.gold_answer: No. Maternity is not available on Bronze at any sum insured; it is available on Silver, Gold and Platinum.

v1.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
v1.answer: Waiting periods require continuous coverage from the initial policy commencement date before claims become payable [1][3], and pre-existing conditions are subject to specific rules if diagnosed within 48 months prior to the start date [2][5]. The sources do not state the specific waiting period duration for pre-existing diseases.
v1.gold_answer: 36 months of continuous coverage. A rider can reduce it to 24 or 12 months if bought at inception or first renewal.

v1.question: How long is the grace period for an annual policy?
v1.answer: The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1].
v1.gold_answer: 30 days for annual policies (15 days for instalment policies). Cover does not operate during the grace period; it only preserves continuity of waiting periods and no-claim bonus.

v1.question: How many hospitals are in the Aurora network?
v1.answer: Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1].
v1.gold_answer: 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026, though the app locator is the authoritative live list.

v1.question: What is the no-claim bonus on Gold?
v1.answer: Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. If a claim is made, the bonus is not reduced; it only stops accumulating for that specific year [1].
v1.gold_answer: 25% of base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100%. A claim stops accumulation for that year but does not reduce the bonus.

v1.question: Can I claim for IVF treatment?
v1.answer: No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment, as IVF, infertility, and assisted reproduction are listed as permanent treatment-related exclusions [1].
v1.gold_answer: No. Infertility treatment, assisted reproduction and IVF are permanent exclusions on all plans.

v1.question: What is the cataract sub-limit on Gold?
v1.answer: The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Aurora Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].
v1.gold_answer: Rs 75,000 per eye.

v1.question: Who can I escalate to if Aurora rejects my claim and their internal response is unsatisfactory?
v1.answer: If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [1]. If Aurora's final response remains unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [2].
v1.gold_answer: Escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (14-day response), then to the Insurance Ombudsman for your region within 1 year of the final rejection.

v1.question: How much ambulance cover is there?
v1.answer: Across all plans, road ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [2][3][4][5]. In addition, the Gold plan provides air ambulance cover up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [2].
v1.gold_answer: Rs 5,000 per hospitalisation for road ambulance on all plans. Gold and Platinum additionally cover air ambulance up to Rs 2,50,000 per year within India on prior authorisation.

v1.question: Is mental illness covered?
v1.answer: In-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1].
v1.gold_answer: Yes. In-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017, subject only to the 30-day initial waiting period.

v1.question: What is the free-look period?
v1.answer: The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A new policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or within 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. The policyholder will receive a premium refund minus the proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [1][4].
v1.gold_answer: 15 days from receipt of the policy document, or 30 days if sold through distance marketing.

v1.question: How many wellness points do I get for completing an annual health check-up?
v1.answer: You earn 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].
v1.gold_answer: 150 points.

v1.question: What is a day-care procedure?
v1.answer: A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advance, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [1]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [1].
v1.gold_answer: A procedure requiring less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advance, and therefore payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement. Out-patient treatment is not a day-care procedure.

v1.question: Within how many hours must a hospital notify Aurora of an emergency admission for cashless?
v1.answer: For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
v1.gold_answer: Within 24 hours of admission.

v1.question: Does Aurora use a TPA?
v1.answer: No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
v1.gold_answer: No. Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator.

v1.question: What is the minimum number of beds a facility needs to count as a hospital?
v1.answer: To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1][2].
v1.gold_answer: At least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, and at least 15 elsewhere.

v1.question: I am on Silver with a 5 lakh sum insured and took a room at Rs 15,000 per day. Will everything be paid?
v1.answer: No, everything will not be paid in full [1]. On a Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured, which is ₹10,000 per day [1][2]. Because the ₹15,000 daily room charge exceeds this limit, a proportionate deduction applies with an eligibility ratio of 0.667 (10,000 ÷ 15,000) [1].
v1.gold_answer: No. The Silver room-rent limit is 2% of 5,00,000 = Rs 10,000/day, so an eligibility ratio of 0.667 is applied by proportionate deduction to all room-linked charges (room, surgeon, anaesthetist, nursing, OT, investigations). Pharmacy and consumables are not reduced.

v1.question: My mother is 63 and I want to add her to my policy. Which plans allow it and what changes?
v1.answer: Dependent parents can be covered under the Silver plan (at an extra premium) as well as the Gold and Platinum plans, but cannot be added under the Bronze plan [2][3]. When adding a parent, the policy premium changes because it is determined by the age of the eldest member covered, which often makes adding them to a floater more expensive than taking out an individual senior-citizen policy [4].
v1.gold_answer: Dependent parents can be added on Silver (at extra premium), Gold and Platinum, but not on Bronze. Premium is set by the eldest member's age, and on Silver a 10% co-payment applies to every claim once the eldest insured is above 60. Aurora must present a separate senior-citizen policy as an alternative in writing.

v1.question: I am switching from another insurer. Will my 3 years of waiting period carry over if I increase my sum insured?
v1.answer: Waiting periods already served with a previous Indian insurer carry over on portability, but only up to the sum insured of the previous policy, including its accrued no-claim bonus [1][3]. Any increase or excess in the sum insured is subject to fresh waiting periods on the incremental amount [1][2].
v1.gold_answer: Waiting-period credit carries over only up to the sum insured of the previous policy including its accrued no-claim bonus. The incremental sum insured is subject to fresh waiting periods. Apply 45-60 days before the existing renewal date.

v1.question: My baby was born last week. What do I need to do and by when?
v1.answer: To continue cover beyond 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the newborn to the policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth [2]. Adding the newborn within this 90-day window is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting, whereas after it, the child is treated as a fresh applicant [1][2].
v1.gold_answer: The newborn is covered from day one within the maternity limit for the first 90 days. To continue cover beyond that, inform Aurora and add the child as a dependent within 90 days of birth, which is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting. After 90 days the child is treated as a fresh applicant.

v1.question: Can I get an out-patient physiotherapy session reimbursed on Bronze?

v1.gold_answer: No. Out-patient treatment is not covered under any base plan, and the OPD rider is not available on Bronze.

v1.question: I had a claim last year on Silver. What happens to my accumulated no-claim bonus?
v1.answer: Under the Aurora Silver plan, a claim in any year reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points [1]. It does not reset the accumulated bonus to zero [1].
v1.gold_answer: On Silver a claim reduces the accumulated bonus by 10 percentage points; it does not reset to zero. Silver accrues 10% per claim-free year up to 50%.

v1.question: How much would a caesarean cost me out of pocket on Gold if the hospital bills 1,60,000?

v1.question: Is knee replacement covered immediately after I buy the policy?

v1.question: What is the total maximum discount I can get on premium?

v1.question: I want cashless at a hospital that turns out to be an excluded provider. What are my options?

A claim from an excluded provider is only payable on reimbursement if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [2].

v2.answer: Knee joint replacement is generally not covered immediately, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [2][4]. However, if the knee replacement is required following an accidental injury, it is covered immediately from day one [1][2][4].

v2.question: What is the total maximum discount I can get on premium?
v2.answer: Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. The wellness discount (up to 15% at renewal based on wellness points) is applied last after the 30% cap and is the only discount that may exceed it [1][3].
v2.gold_answer: Discounts are capped at 30% of base premium, but the wellness discount of up to 15% is applied after the cap and is the only discount permitted to exceed it.

v2.question: I want cashless at a hospital that turns out to be an excluded provider. What are my options?
v2.answer: Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider and will be denied at pre-authorisation [1][2]. Your only option is reimbursement with pre-approval, which is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [2]. If eligible, you must pay the hospital yourself, notify Aurora within 48 hours of an emergency admission, and submit your claim within 30 days of discharge [4].
v2.gold_answer: Cashless is not available at an excluded provider. The claim is payable on reimbursement only if the admission was a genuine emergency with no reachable alternative facility, and pre-approval is required.

v2.question: How many days do I have to respond to a query Aurora raises on my claim?
v2.answer: For health insurance claims, you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond [1]. For Aurora Motor Insurance claims, the deadline to respond to an Aurora query is 30 days from the date of the query [4].

v2.question: How far in advance must a planned cashless admission be notified?

v2.question: How long does Aurora take to settle a reimbursement claim?
v2.answer: Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. v2.question: Which plans have no co-payment?

v2.question: Compare the pre- and post-hospitalisation windows across all four plans.
v2.answer: Across the four plans, pre-hospitalisation cover is 30 days for Bronze, 45 days for Silver, 60 days for Gold, and 90 days for Platinum [1]. Post-hospitalisation cover is 60 days for Bronze, 90 days for Silver, 120 days for Gold, and 180 days for Platinum [1].

v2.question: Which plan should I buy if I want no room-rent sub-limit and cover for my parents-in-law?

v2.question: List everything that is excluded relating to dental treatment.
v2.answer: Dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded under Aurora indemnity plans unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [1][3]. v2.question: If I skip paying on time, how long before I lose everything I've built up?
v2.answer: For health insurance policies, you will lose your accumulated benefits once the grace period expires, which is 30 days from the renewal due date for annual policies and 15 days for policies paid in instalments [1][4]. If you renew after this grace period ends, the policy is treated as fresh: all waiting periods restart, accumulated no-claim bonuses are lost, and fresh underwriting applies [1].
